title: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected
shortDescription: Crankshaft variation indicates misfires across multiple or random cylinders.
fullDescription: P0300 sets when the ECM detects misfires distributed across more than one cylinder, or no clear pattern. The crankshaft position sensor watches for the deceleration signature that occurs when a cylinder fails to fire. Multiple-cylinder misfire often indicates a system-wide cause — fuel pressure, ignition coil pack on coil-on-plug-pair platforms, MAF, vacuum leak, or low compression — rather than a single bad coil or plug.
safetyImpact: Catalytic converter damage if MIL flashes (active misfire). Reduce engine load until repaired.

causes.cause: Worn spark plugs (gap drift, electrode wear)
Vacuum leak (intake gasket, PCV, brake booster hose)
Low fuel pressure (failing pump, plugged filter)
Contaminated MAF sensor
Bad gasoline (water, ethanol incompatibility)
Carbon buildup on intake valves (DI engines)
Failing ignition coil pack (waste-spark systems)
EGR valve stuck open at idle

fixSteps.title: Read freeze frame and misfire counts
fixSteps.instruction: View per-cylinder misfire counters. If counts are roughly equal across cylinders, suspect a system-wide cause (fuel/air/ignition shared component).

fixSteps.title: Inspect spark plugs
fixSteps.instruction: Pull all plugs. Check for proper gap (spec varies, often 0.040-0.044 in), uniform color, no oil/coolant contamination.

fixSteps.title: Test fuel pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Connect gauge at rail. Verify static pressure within spec, watch for drop under load.

fixSteps.title: Check for vacuum leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Smoke test intake or use propane near gaskets. Look at idle fuel trims — over +10% LTFT suggests leak.

fixSteps.title: Compression / leakdown
fixSteps.instruction: If still misfiring after tune-up, run compression test on all cylinders. Mechanical issues (valve, ring) need internal repair.

faq.q: Flashing vs steady CEL?
faq.a: Flashing = active misfire damaging catalyst. Pull over and reduce load. Steady = misfire occurred but is not currently active.

faq.q: Should I drive with P0300?
faq.a: Short, low-load drive only. Continued operation can destroy catalytic converters costing $1000+.

title: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
shortDescription: Cylinder 1 misfire — crankshaft variation localized to one cylinder.
fullDescription: P0301 sets when the ECM detects misfires concentrated on cylinder 1. The crankshaft sensor measures the speed dip during each cylinder's power stroke; when cylinder 1's signature falls below threshold, the misfire counter increments. Single-cylinder misfire usually points to ignition (coil/plug), injector, or compression on that specific cylinder.
safetyImpact: Active flashing MIL = catalyst damage risk. Avoid sustained driving.

causes.cause: Worn or fouled spark plug, cylinder 1
Failed ignition coil, cylinder 1 (COP)
Stuck or clogged fuel injector, cylinder 1
Low compression cylinder 1 (burnt valve, worn rings, head gasket)
Carbon on intake valve, cylinder 1 (DI engines)
Vacuum leak local to cylinder 1 (intake runner gasket)
Wiring fault to coil or injector

symptoms: Rough idle, vibration felt at steering column
Possible fuel smell from increased unburnt HC

fixSteps.title: Swap coil and plug
fixSteps.instruction: Move cylinder 1 ignition coil to a neighboring cylinder and the plug to a different bore. Recheck — if misfire moves with coil, replace coil. If with plug, replace plug.

fixSteps.title: Test injector
fixSteps.instruction: Measure injector resistance (typically 11-16 ohms saturated, 1-3 ohms peak-and-hold). Use NOID light or scope to confirm pulse. Swap injector position to confirm.

fixSteps.title: Compression test
fixSteps.instruction: Pull plug on cylinder 1, screw in gauge. Crank with throttle open — should be within 10% of other cylinders. Low compression = cylinder leakdown next.

fixSteps.title: Cylinder leakdown
fixSteps.instruction: Bring cylinder 1 to TDC compression, apply 100 psi shop air. Listen for hiss at intake (valve), exhaust (valve), oil cap (rings), or radiator (head gasket).

fixSteps.title: Repair root cause
fixSteps.instruction: Replace coil, plug, injector, or address mechanical fault. Use OEM ignition components on modern engines.

faq.q: How do I know which is cylinder 1?
faq.a: Consult engine layout for the specific make. Many manufacturers stamp cylinder numbers on the valve cover or intake.

title: Ignition Coil Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction
shortDescription: Generic ignition coil primary/secondary circuit fault.
fullDescription: P0350 is the umbrella code for an ignition coil circuit fault when the ECM cannot identify which specific coil. Modern vehicles set P0351-P0362 for specific cylinders; P0350 typically appears on older multi-coil systems or when the fault is shared across coils.
safetyImpact: Possible misfire, catalyst damage if active.

causes.cause: Failed ignition coil shared driver
Failed ignition module (waste spark)
Power supply fault to coil rail

fixSteps.title: Verify coil power
fixSteps.instruction: All coils should see battery voltage on power pin during cranking and run.

fixSteps.title: Scope coil drivers
fixSteps.instruction: Each driver should pulse low to ground during normal operation.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed coil/module
fixSteps.instruction: Use OEM. Apply dielectric grease on COP boots.

title: Ignition Coil A (Cylinder 1) Primary/Secondary Circuit
shortDescription: Cylinder 1 ignition coil primary/secondary circuit electrical fault.
fullDescription: P0351 sets when the ECM detects an electrical fault on the cylinder 1 ignition coil — open coil, shorted primary, or driver-side wiring problem. The ECM monitors current waveform on the coil driver; deviation triggers the code. Distinct from a misfire (P0301) — this is purely electrical and may exist without a current misfire if the coil only fails intermittently.
safetyImpact: Probable misfire under load with associated catalyst damage risk.

causes.cause: Failed ignition coil on cylinder 1 (open or shorted primary winding)
Damaged or oil-contaminated coil boot, cylinder 1
Open or chafed wiring between ECM and coil
Corroded coil connector pins
Failed ECM driver (rare)

fixSteps.title: Inspect coil and boot
fixSteps.instruction: Remove coil from cylinder 1. Inspect boot for cracks, oil intrusion, carbon track. Replace boot if damaged.

fixSteps.title: Coil resistance test

title: Misfire Detected — Fueling Disabled
shortDescription: ECM has disabled fuel injection on cylinders with persistent misfire to protect the catalyst.
fullDescription: P0363 sets when the ECM has accumulated enough misfire counts on one or more cylinders to risk catalyst damage; it then disables fuel injection on the affected cylinder(s) until the next key cycle. Always accompanied by a P030x companion identifying the offending cylinder. Treat as urgent — driving with cylinders disabled stresses the engine.
safetyImpact: Engine running on reduced cylinders. Reduced power, increased vibration.

causes.cause: Persistent misfire on a specific cylinder (see companion P030x)
Severe ignition or fuel system fault
Mechanical failure (compression loss)

fixSteps.title: Read companion code
fixSteps.instruction: Identify which cylinder triggered shutdown via accompanying P030x.

fixSteps.title: Diagnose root cause
fixSteps.instruction: Follow misfire diagnostic flow on the affected cylinder.

fixSteps.title: Repair and clear
fixSteps.instruction: Repair, then clear codes — fueling re-enables next key cycle.

faq.q: Will fuel turn back on automatically?
faq.a: Yes — after key cycle. But misfire will return if root cause is not fixed.

title: Reserved by SAE J2012 — Manufacturer Misfire Subset
shortDescription: Manufacturer-defined misfire subset code, reserved range.
fullDescription: P0364 is a generic SAE-reserved code that some manufacturers use for advanced misfire detection states (e.g., misfire detected but not yet exceeding catalyst-damage threshold). Behavior is platform-specific — consult OEM service information. Treat any misfire-related code as urgent diagnostically.
safetyImpact: Possible misfire developing.

causes.cause: Early-stage misfire, see companion codes
Spark plug or coil degradation
Marginal fuel pressure

fixSteps.title: Read OEM-specific service info
fixSteps.instruction: Behavior varies — consult factory service manual for the exact platform.

fixSteps.title: Inspect tune-up parts
fixSteps.instruction: Pull plugs, inspect coils, check fuel pressure.

title: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire — Direct-Injection Carbon Pattern
shortDescription: Random misfire pattern characteristic of intake-valve carbon on DI engines.
fullDescription: Same SAE definition as P0300, but covers the specific failure mode common on direct-injection engines (VW/Audi TSI/TFSI, BMW N54/N55/N20, Ford EcoBoost, Hyundai/Kia GDI) after 60,000-100,000 miles: carbon deposits accumulate on intake valves because no fuel washes them. Misfire occurs random across cylinders depending on which valves seat poorly that cycle. Standard tune-up parts pass tests but misfire continues — diagnosis requires borescope of intake ports.
safetyImpact: Catalyst damage from sustained misfire.

causes.cause: Heavy intake-valve carbon (DI engines)
PCV system over-feeding oil mist into intake
Worn high-pressure fuel pump (DI)
Failing low-pressure lift pump
Carbon-fouled or worn spark plugs (DI engines run hotter)

symptoms: Cold-start rough idle that smooths warm

fixSteps.title: Borescope intake ports
fixSteps.instruction: Remove intake manifold (or use borescope through removed coil/injector access). Visually confirm carbon depth on intake valves.

fixSteps.title: Walnut-blast intake valves
fixSteps.instruction: With pistons at TDC of compression to seal valves, walnut-shell media blast each port. Vacuum debris between cylinders. Standard service every 60-80k mi on DI engines.

fixSteps.title: Replace HPFP if low rail pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm fuel rail pressure under load matches commanded value. Replace HPFP if low.

fixSteps.title: Inspect PCV / oil separator
fixSteps.instruction: DI engines often have oil separator failures dumping mist into intake. Replace separator if found leaking.

faq.q: Can fuel additive fix this?
faq.a: Limited — port-injected detergents wash valves, but DI engines bypass the intake valves entirely, so carbon must be cleaned mechanically.

faq.q: How often is walnut blasting needed?
faq.a: Typically 60,000-100,000 miles on most DI engines.

title: Engine Misfire Detected on Startup (First 1000 Revolutions)
shortDescription: Misfire detected during the first 1000 crank revolutions after start.
fullDescription: P0316 is a Ford-pioneered code now widely used: the ECM watches misfire counts during the first 1000 crank revolutions after engine start. If the count exceeds threshold, P0316 sets along with the specific cylinder code. Typical causes are cold-stiff injectors, weak coils, or low-compression cylinders that recover after warm-up.
safetyImpact: Cold-start emissions exceedance; possible catalyst damage if misfire is severe.

causes.cause: Cold-weak ignition coil that works hot
Sticky fuel injector (clears with fuel flow)
Carbon-fouled spark plug (recovers when hot)
Low compression cylinder masked by warm expansion
Insufficient cold-start fuel pressure

symptoms: Rough idle for first 30 seconds after cold start

fixSteps.title: Read companion P030x code
fixSteps.instruction: Identifies the specific cylinder. Focus diagnosis there.

fixSteps.title: Cold-start coil/plug swap
fixSteps.instruction: Swap suspect coil or plug to neighbor cylinder. Let cool overnight. Cold-start next morning — see if misfire follows.

fixSteps.title: Check fuel pressure at cold start
fixSteps.instruction: Connect gauge before first start of the day. Pressure should rise within 1-2 seconds and stay in spec.

fixSteps.title: Cold compression test if persistent
fixSteps.instruction: Test compression cold (engine sat overnight). A cylinder lower than others when cold but recovering when warm is a worn-ring/bore issue.

repairTime: 1-3 hours (test) up to multiple sessions for cold reproduction

faq.q: Why does it only set in the morning?
faq.a: Components contract when cold; weak ones lose contact or have insufficient flow until warm-up.
